title: Comparison star Gaia DR3 1648326843826192768 (G = 12.5)

spectrum.method: Forced ePSF photometry on native pixels at the motion-corrected (followed) position in every exposure; wavelength from the spectral WCS at that pixel; inverse-variance means in the 102 SPHEREx/SPIFF bins.

fixed_vs_follow.note: Measured at one fixed sky position, the source keeps 100% of the flux recovered by following its motion (median over 71 bins).

templates.library: SPIFF SPHEREx templates (Gagné et al. 2026; M4–Y0 field, low-gravity and subdwarf grids)
templates.reason: Closest library template is K0, which is outside the ultracool-dwarf domain this library is built for; treat as indicative only.

naive.description: Every exposure in time order, regardless of wavelength. Because SPHEREx sees a different wavelength in each exposure, most of this apparent change is the source spectrum, not time variability.

matched.description: Flux in the same SPHEREx wavelength bin compared between visits. Only this comparison can reveal true time variability.

hypotheses.name: Stationary astronomical source
evidence: No significant motion (0.2 sigma); 3-sigma limit about 131 mas/yr.

hypotheses.name: Moving astronomical source
evidence: Measured positions are consistent with no motion at the achieved precision.

hypotheses.name: Blended or overlapping sources
evidence: No Gaia DR3 neighbour within 2 SPHEREx pixels.

hypotheses.name: Instrumental or processing artifact
evidence: Detected in 102 independent exposures across 3 visits, on multiple detectors and wavelengths.

hypotheses.name: Known solar-system object
evidence: PARALLAX does not yet query solar-system ephemerides (e.g. JPL Horizons); not evaluated.

summary.headline: No significant motion or variability detected.
summary.one_liner: Measured in 102 exposures with no significant position change. No ultracool-dwarf template fits well, as expected for an ordinary star.

limitations: SPHEREx pixels are 6.15 arcsec; sources closer than about 1 pixel are measured as one blend.
Positions are registered to Gaia DR3 field stars with a pure shift per exposure; residual distortion is absorbed into an empirical error floor.
Fluxes use the median pixel solid angle (OMEGA_MEDIAN) and the release ePSF; absolute calibration uncertainties of a few percent are not propagated.
follow_up: No follow-up required for this known source.
